# read_A: pp. 63–65 (leaves n64–n66), established from the images

Line counts: p. 63 has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with ༄༅༔ ༔ (checked at ×3: the ornament ༄༅ with its ༔, a gap, then ༔ཀྱཻ). p. 64 has five lines (a leaf back, no ornament). p. 65 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔ནས༔, checked). That makes 15 print lines. The witness's line breaks match the print on all 15.

**Start of the part.** 63.1 opens with the ornament and then ༔ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ སྐུ་དེ་དག་ཀྱང་མི་ཆེ་བ༔ … This is the sentence about the size of the deities, which part 006 left for p. 63. So the part begins at 63.1, as planned.

Method: line bands were found from the row profile. The headlines are at n64 y≈105/165/220/272/327 and n65 ≈175/232/285/338/393. n66 is rotated by about 1°: its headlines run from y≈103/158/213/265/320 at x 240 to ≈131/188/246/303/360 at x 1640. Its bands were cropped with that slope. Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS). Doubtful syllables were enlarged to ×5–×8, with pixel dumps (threshold 128) where needed. I checked every ༔ on the three pages for a tsheg, using montages at ×5 and, for every ང/ངོ before ༔, a ×10 crop or a pixel dump. I checked the end of every line by pixel dump between the last letter and the frame.

- 63.3 སེམས་མ་དང་༔: a separate 5×5 px blob at headline height (x 1305–1310), with white on both sides at row 219. Tsheg.
- 64.2 and 64.4 འོང་ངོ་༔: ×10. A triangular wedge stands at the top left of the ༔ ring, between the end of the ངོ head and the ring. It is joined to the ring and is absent from ring tops elsewhere (e.g. 64.5). Read as a fused tsheg. These are close calls.
- 65.2, 65.4 and 65.5 འོང་ངོ་༔: pixel dumps. A separate 4–6 px blob at headline height (x 717–722, 1765–1768, 938–944) stands between ང and the ring. Clear tshegs.

Every other ༔ on the three pages has no tsheg. I checked all of them by montage at ×5: བུ༔, བ༔, པ༔, ཏེ༔, བས༔, ཤིག༔, ནས༔, སྟེ༔, ཅིག༔, དུ༔.

- 63.4 འཆར་དུ་འོང་བས༔ (not ངོ).

## [?] (1)

- 63.3 (line end) **རྫོགས[?]**: the -གས ligature is certain. The doubt is the subjoined letter under ར, which has three bars and no tsa-phru I can see. The witness typed ཇ (རྗོ). But the place where a tsa-phru would stand, at the top right of the subjoined letter, lies under the long naro and the ར head, so its absence proves nothing. The sense (and the other recension: དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ཐམས་ཅད་དུས་གཅིག་ལ་རྫོགས་པར་འཆར) wants རྫོགས. If the drafter judges the image to show ཇ, then it is a misprint, and the note should give the print's reading as རྗོགས.

Close calls not marked [?]:
- 64.5 (line end) ཀ་, 65.1 (line end) ལེ་, 65.5 (line end) ལས་: each line ends in filler dots. In 64.5 they are fused into a dotted rule that starts 1 px after ཀ. A tsheg cannot be told apart from the first filler dot, so it is read as a tsheg, as read_C did at 61.x. If the drafter reads none, the joins need:
  - `# fix: ཐུགས་ཀ༄༅༔ ༔ནས => ཐུགས་ཀ་༄༅༔ ༔ནས` (64.5→65.1, across the leaf-front ornament)
  - `# fix: ཐིག་ལེདང་ཐིག => ཐིག་ལེ་དང་ཐིག` (65.1→65.2)
  - and a fix for ལས at the join to p. 66 (Reader B's first line).
- The fused tshegs before ༔ at 63.1, 64.2 and 64.4 (see above).
- 64.2 སྦུབ (see the table). If the drafter keeps སྤུབ, the sense is the same ("turned upside down").

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

```
# fix: ཡབ་ཀྱིཆ་འཛིན => ཡབ་ཀྱི་ཆ་འཛིན
# fix: རྫོགས[?]པར་འཆར => རྫོགས[?]་པར་འཆར
# fix: ཕྲན་གྱིསབརྒྱན་པ་ཅིག => ཕྲན་གྱིས་བརྒྱན་པ་ཅིག
# fix: ཐིག་ལེ་སྔོནཔོ་འོད => ཐིག་ལེ་སྔོན་པོ་འོད
```
These are the joins 63.2→63.3, 63.3→63.4, 64.3→64.4 and 64.4→64.5. In each, the last letter meets the frame or clear space with no tsheg. Write the second fix without "[?]" once the reading is settled.

The 63.3 ligature is written out as གས in read_A.txt, following the precedent of part 002. It needs no fix line, but the drafter may want to note it once.

There are no other line-end abbreviations (པའཾ, ལཾ, ྶ) or ནམཁའ-type contractions on these pages.

Tsheg status at the borders: 63.1 opens with the ornament ༄༅༔ ༔. The last line, 65.5, ends ལས་ (a close call; see above). The join 63.5→64.1 (འཆར་ | དུ) is fine.

## Suspected misprints

1. 63.3 རྫོགས / རྗོགས: see [?]. If ཇ is read, it is a misprint for རྫོགས (moderate certainty that the print has ཛ at all). The sense allows only རྫོགས.
2. 63.5 ལྟ་བུ་**མེ**་རེ་རེ: the image clearly shows མེ, but the syllable makes no good sense here ("like rays of sunlight spun into a cord, ? one by one"). The other recension lacks it. Kept, note only.
3. 65.4 མཚེར་བ beside 64.3 འཚེར་བ: a spelling variant of the same verb, not a misprint. Kept.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: ཡིན་བས (for པས), ཕོར་པ (for ཕོར་བ), ཀྱཻ.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- 63.1: print རྒྱན་ཁ་དོག་བཞུགས་ཚུལ ("ornaments, colours, manner of sitting"); other recension རྒྱན་ཆ་ལུགས་ཁ་དོག… (adds "dress").
- 63.2: **print ལྔ་ལྔའི་ཟུང་གིས་ཁྱབ་པ ("pervaded by pairs of five"); other recension …ཟུང་གིས་བརྒྱན་པ ("adorned")**.
- 63.2: print འོད་ལྔའི་ཚོམ་བུས་མུ་ཁྱུད ("a rim of clusters of five-coloured light"); other recension འོད་ལྔའི་མུ་ཁྱུད.
- 63.3: print ཐམས་ཅད་གཅིག་ལ་རྫོགས་པར ("complete in one"); other recension ཐམས་ཅད་དུས་གཅིག་ལ ("all at one time").
- 63.4: print འཆར་དུ་འོང་བས༔ དེ… (clause chain); other recension འོང་ངོ༔ (sentence ends). Same sense.
- 63.5: print འོད་ཟེར་ཕྲ་ལ་དྭངས་པ; other recension ཤིན་ཏུ་ཕྲ་ལ ("very fine").
- 63.5: **print ཉི་མའི་འོད་ཟེར་སྦ་ཐག་དྲིལ་བ་ལྟ་བུ ("like sun-rays rolled into a cane-cord/twine"); other recension བ་ཐག་སྦྲེལ་བ ("joined into a rope")**. Print adds མེ (see misprints).
- 64.1: other recension དང་པོར; print དང་པོ. Same.
- 64.2: print སྣམ་བུ་ཅིག…སྙིང་ཁ; other recension སྣམ་བུ་གཅིག…སྙིང་ཀ. Same.
- 64.2: print སྣམ་བུ་དེའི་སྟེང་དུ ("on that strip"); other recension ནང་དུ ("within").
- 64.2–3: print ལྡན་པ་མེ་ལོང་ཁ་སྦུབ་པ་ཙམ་པ ("the size of an upturned mirror"); other recension ལྡན་པ༔ མེ་ལོང…ཙམ. Same.
- 64.4: print བརྒྱན་པ་ཅིག་འཆར ("one adorned … appears"); other recension བརྒྱན་པ་འཆར. Same.
- 64.4–5: **print ཐིག་ལེ་སྔོན་པོ་འོད་དང་ལྡན་པ་དཔེར་ན་གཡུའི་ཕོར་པ ("a blue sphere with light, like a turquoise bowl"); other recension ཐིག་ལེ་མཐིང་ཀ་གཡུའི་ཕོར་བ (no "with light", no "for example")**.
- 65.1: print ཐིག་ལེ་དང་ཐིག་ཕྲན་གྱིས་བརྒྱན་པ ("adorned with spheres and small spheres"); other recension ཐིག་ལེ་ཐིག་ཕྲན་དང་བཅས་པ ("together with…"). Same sense.
- 65.3–5 (the red sphere of Amitābha and the summing up): the bo.wikipedia text breaks off into a different passage here (…དམར་ལ་འཚེར་བ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་དང་ཐིག་ཕྲན་གྱིས་སྤྲས་པ… then the hungry-ghost light), so there is no comparison for 65.3–5.
